articles.title: Quantum computing’s first real-world payoff may come in energy, not drug discovery
articles.summary: But quantum software, which uses algorithms designed to solve complex problems faster than conventional computers, is already being tested on a more immediate challenge: the energy transition, from keeping power grids stable to finding better materials for solar cells and hydrogen production. Phasecraft, a quantum software company founded in Bristol, England, in 2019, is one of the firms putting the technology to work in energy.

articles.title: Anthropic’s record IPO collides with tech’s worst week on Wall Street since 2020
articles.summary: Startup investor Ben Narasin is so jazzed about Anthropic's blockbuster IPO that he's planning a party later this month at his Silicon Valley home. Investors and analysts spent the week debating whether Anthropic will trade alongside AI hardware, as it's reliant on advanced chips, memory and data centers, or whether it will stand alone as the first public pure-play AI developer and a company that's achieved unrivaled growth in less than six years of existence.
